equity.level_reason: Race and SES (education, income) are reported as group results and described, e.g. 'Blacks and Hispanics reported receiving less advice than did whites', with causes discussed. The contrasts are side-by-side percentages with no computed difference, so the level is capped at 2.

level_alternative.reason: The editorial frames the racial difference and offers causes; a reader who counts the text's 'less advice' statements as quantified would give 3, but no difference is computed.

equity.equity_measurement: Race and SES results are side-by-side percentages with no computed contrast; several race and plan-type rows lack estimates for sample size under 100 (table notes, OCR). Race and income exclude different respondent counts (5,249 and 15,691, per table notes, OCR).

notes: Survey weights produce every estimate, so they are the primary procedure; no regression, standardization or interaction is reported. Tables 1 and 2 are OCR-only, so their numbers are unverified; the CI test against the 62.5% national average is ancillary.
view_issues: Text says women's advice rates are higher 'across all visit categories', but per Table 2 OCR men exceed women at 5 visits (76.8 vs 75.7). Tables 1-2 are OCR-only with garbled alignment; numbers unverified.
